title: Python's property(): Add Managed Attributes to Your Classes
description: Use Python's property() to add managed attributes to your classes, with validation, computed values, and caching, without breaking your API.
summary: The @property decorator simplifies the management of attributes in your Python classes . It allows you to control attribute access, enabling features such as data validation, lazy evaluation , and the creation of backward-compatible APIs without modifying the class’s public interface.
takeaways: Object-Oriented Python Live Course: Want to practice using @property to protect your class invariants in a real project?

In Real Python’s Object-Oriented Python live course, you build a complete simulator with an instructor, adding properties, alternative constructors, and other OOP tools only when the design needs them.
